proposer_argument.content:
POSITION
Claim A is correct - Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived.

EVIDENCE REVIEW
Claim A: The Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived was Moctezuma II, based on historical records of the Aztec Empire's leadership during the 1519 arrival of Hernán Cortés.
Claim B: Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh was appointed by the Spanish as one of the Aztec rulers after their arrival - this claim is not supported by historical evidence. Andrés de Tapia was a Spanish chronicler and conquistador, not an Aztec ruler.

REASONING
The core issue is identifying who held leadership of the Aztec Empire at the moment of Spanish contact in 1519. Historical documentation consistently shows Moctezuma II as the reigning tlatoani (ruler) during this period. The claim that Andrés de Tapia served as an Aztec ruler is factually incorrect, as Tapia was a Spanish participant in the conquest, not an indigenous ruler. The conflict is resolved by establishing the correct historical leadership at the time of contact.

SOURCE BASIS
The supplied claims themselves contain the key information - Claim A correctly identifies Moctezuma II as ruler during Spanish arrival, while Claim B incorrectly attributes rulership to Andrés de Tapia, who was documented as a Spanish chronicler and conquistador rather than an Aztec ruler.

CONCLUSION
Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived in 1519.
